title: Probabilistic windowed batching advisor and safe-apply pipeline
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Design and implement a probabilistic windowed batching recommendation engine that profiles live workloads (sketching short-term inter-arrival distributions and sequence-length histograms), produces conservative batch-size and batch-horizon suggestions, and applies them via a safe-apply pipeline that supports shadow evaluation, gradual rollouts, and automated rollback triggers. The feature must respect prefix/KV cache interactions, be quantization-aware (avoid suggestions that regress quantized kernels), and integrate with Console for explainability and a one-click revert.
acceptance_criteria: Agent computes per-workload 'windowed inter-arrival' sketch and per-route sequence-length histogram within 5% of sampled offline profiler for >95% of routes
Recommendation engine outputs a top-3 ranked set of (batch_size, max_horizon, kv_cache_policy) suggestions with expected token-cost delta and latency P95 impact estimates
Safe-apply pipeline can perform: shadow-apply, canary (1% -> 10% -> 50%), and full apply with automated rollback on defined SLO regressions
Console surfaces the recommendation explanation, change diff, and a one-click revert; telemetry shows pre/post cost and latency breakdown per token
Automated rollback triggers activate if latency P95 increases by >20% or error-rate increases by >1% absolute within the first 30 minutes of any stage
End-to-end integration tests covering shadow mode, canary ramp, and forced rollback scenarios exist in CI with synthetic workload replay
implementation_notes: Profiling: use lightweight Count-Min sketches for inter-arrival times + fixed-bin histograms for sequence lengths; keep RAM footprint < 2MB per route
Recommendation logic: probabilistic model that computes expected cost and latency using empirical PMFs from sketches and a small parametric latency model calibrated per-node-type
Safety fences: hard caps per-customer configured in RBAC; do not suggest changes that increase per-token compute by >10% in baseline throughput scenarios
KV cache interplay: flag suggestions that reduce cache hit ratio by estimating prefix overlap change; if estimated hit-ratio loss > 5% mark as 'requires manual review'
Quantization: integrate with kernel-compatibility table to avoid batch sizes that trigger slow fallback kernels on older drivers
Rollout: implement shadow-apply by duplicating requests to candidate config with sampling; collect diffs in a dedicated shadow metrics namespace
Telemetry: emit 'recommendation_id' across traces and metrics; Console will use this to join pre/post windows
Performance: recommend incremental scoring during off-peak and only re-evaluate high-variance routes every 5 minutes to limit compute
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal alpha — enable engine for internal services only (shopdev, onboarding) and run shadow-apply for 48h
Phase 1: Beta — select customer cohort (10 tenants) enable canary pipeline with strict rollback thresholds and SLO monitoring
Phase 2: Gradual release — 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 1h observation windows between steps
Phase 3: GA — enable as opt-in in Console and add automatic scheduled re-evaluations
Rollback plan: immediate revert on automated trigger, otherwise manual revert via console revert button; all rollbacks must create a postmortem ticket
telemetry: Emit per-route: pre.batch_p95_latency_ms, post.batch_p95_latency_ms, pre.token_cost, post.token_cost, kv_cache_hit_rate_before, kv_cache_hit_rate_after
Tracing: include recommendation_id and shadow=true tag for shadow traffic
Dashboards: temporary 'prob-windowed-batching' dashboard for initial beta with cost delta heatmap and rollback alarm
